business_problem: Lambda needed to raise token throughput and improve AI-cloud economics, but fixed rack and facility power budgets were leaving GPU capacity stranded and limiting how many nodes could run safely at once.
solution_summary: Lambda validated NVIDIA's DSX AI Factory Platform as an operational layer for power-constrained AI clusters rather than just a benchmark feature. On a five-rack HGX B200 environment, DSX MaxLPS and its Dynamic Power Software monitored GPU and rack-level draw in real time, then redistributed available power so more nodes could run under the same facility ceiling. Operators set policy targets such as 80 or 85 percent of maximum node draw without modifying active workloads, which allowed Lambda to pack additional inference and training nodes into the same footprint while keeping visibility through power-observability dashboards. Because mixed inference and training jobs have different power curves, the system could reclaim capacity that static provisioning leaves idle. That architecture turns power shaping into a control plane for AI-factory utilization, not just a hardware setting, and gives Lambda a path to lower cost per token as clusters scale.

solution_components.name: Dynamic Power Software

data_flow: Training and inference workloads are scheduled onto HGX B200 nodes, where Dynamic Power Software tracks live consumption and DSX MaxLPS applies per-policy power targets. The adjusted node budgets let Lambda run additional servers, and throughput and observability metrics feed back into cluster operations for ongoing tuning.
business_outcome: Lambda increased cluster-wide token throughput by 24 percent, improved performance per watt by 23 percent, raised hybrid inference throughput by 20 percent, and lifted hybrid training throughput by 17 percent without expanding the facility power budget.
